chunks: So, where are you being mislead?!
And from where have you been brought (to this state)?
Be prepared to march to the people who have deviated from the right and do not see it,
have been entangled in wrongdoing and are not corrected.
They are away from the Book,
You are not trustworthy to rely upon,
nor are you holders of honour to be adhered to.
You are very bad in kindling the fire of fighting.
I had to bear a lot of worries from you.
Some day I call you (to jihād) and some day I speak to you in confidence,
you are neither true free men at the time of call, nor trustworthy brothers at the time of speaking in confidence!
ai.seo_question: What criticism does Imam Ali level against the Kharijites in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from the Sermon of the Kharijites, Imam Ali (AS) employs vivid metaphors of disorientation and structural failure to characterize the Kharijites as 'people of confusion' (Qawm Hayara) who are detached from the Quran and unjust in their application of it. This critique highlights the core Shia scholarly view that their deviation stemmed not from piety, but from a rigid, superficial adherence to the text that led to social fragmentation and unreliable allegiance during the Battle of Siffin.
